decision: Reject the current H200 readiness generation before provider creation and require one same-project executable-owner correction.

observed_blockers.evidence: The remote program invokes /work/input/endpoint_entrypoint.py, but that file is absent from the project and from exact_packet().
exact_packet() archives inputs/exact_runner.py at that nested path, while CAPTURE_COMMAND invokes /work/input/exact_runner.py.

The READY artifact promises REPAIR_READY.json and retained-claim recovery, but the owner contains no repair-handshake path and exits after exceptions while leaving a claimed bench without a durable owner.
science_started.json is written before checkpoint validation, image pull, server construction, and server health, rather than immediately before the first real target-tap request.
The readiness loop has no terminal assertion after exhausting its iterations and can continue into the capture request without a successful health response.

preserve: the exact checkpoint, image, c32 workload, training geometry, holdout gate, and one-cycle limit
required_changes: Bind and stage the actual pinned server entrypoint, or invoke the pinned image's proven SGLang server entrypoint directly.
Make the staged exact-runner destination and CAPTURE_COMMAND path identical.
Implement a live retained-claim repair handshake for recoverable pre-science staging, launch, import, API, and server-health defects; never leave an ownerless claim.
Persist launch_attempted before support work and write science_started only after exact runtime identity and server health pass, immediately before the first capture request.
Fail the health wait promptly on server exit and require a positive health response before capture.
Preserve completed capture before training and retrieve its typed terminal and manifest before any later consumer repair.
Re-run local syntax and command-graph checks, then atomically replace H200_CAPTURE_TRAIN_READY.json with the corrected owner sha256 and this director repair sha256.
